Use the **nCoV_simple** dataset for the following questions.

1. In class, we used parametric bootstrap (with a Weibull model) to study the $90th$ percentile of the incubation period.  We now use the **nonparametric bootstrap** to study the $90th$ percentile.

    a. What is the $90th$ percentile of the incubation period among patients in the dataset?  Recall, in R, you can use the **quantile** function.

    b. Obtain $B=1000$ (nonparametric) bootstrap samples; record the $90th$ percentile of each bootstrap sample.  What is the SD of the $90th$ percentile based on your bootstrap samples?

    c. Compared to the median (we have estimated its SD in class), does the $90th$ percentile have more or less variation?
    d. Obtain a $95\%$ confidence interval for the $90th$ percentile of the incubation period.

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ncov_simple <- read.csv("../all_lectures/nCoV_simple.csv")

# a
quantile(ncov_simple$incubation, probs = 0.9)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  90% 
6.785 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# b
bootsize <- 1000
bootresult <- rep(NA, bootsize)
for (i in seq_len(bootsize)) {
  bootresult[i] <- quantile(sample(ncov_simple$incubation, replace = TRUE), probs = 0.9)
}
sd(bootresult)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 1.091851
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# The 90th percentile has more variation than the median.

# d
quantile(bootresult, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
 2.5% 97.5% 
5.500 9.104 
```


:::
:::


</details>



2. Suppose we want to use nonparametric bootstrap to study the **maximum** incubation period.

    a. What is the maximum incubation period among patients in the dataset?

    b. Obtain $B=1000$ bootstrap samples and construct a $95\%$ confidence interval for the maximum incubation period.

    c. Briefly explain why bootstrap does not work well for estimating the maximum incubation period.

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

The maximum incubation period in the dataset is 11 days. The bootstrap confidence interval is 8.5 to 11 days, which underestimates uncertainty because bootstrap samples cannot produce a maximum greater than 11.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# a
max(ncov_simple$incubation)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 11
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# b
bootsize <- 1000
bootresult <- rep(NA, bootsize)
for (i in seq_len(bootsize)) {
  bootresult[i] <- max(sample(ncov_simple$incubation, replace = TRUE))
}
quantile(bootresult, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
 2.5% 97.5% 
  8.5  11.0 
```


:::
:::


</details>

3. In this question, we use parametric bootstrap to obtain confidence intervals for the parameters of a **log-normal model**.

    a. What is the plug-in distribution in this case?
    b. Generate one bootstrap sample from the plug-in distribution and re-fit the log-normal model.  What are the new parameter estimates?

    c. Repeat (b) for 1000 times to obtain 1000 estimates for each of the log-normal model parameters.  Construct $99\%$ confidence intervals for each of the parameters.

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

The plug-in distribution is a log-normal distribution with parameters `meanlog = 1.209` and `sdlog = 0.731`.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# a
library(MASS)
model1 <- fitdistr(ncov_simple$incubation, "lognormal", lower = 0)
model1$estimate
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  meanlog     sdlog 
1.2092543 0.7307774 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# b
samplesize <- nrow(ncov_simple)  # sample size is 50 for the dataset
bootdata <- rlnorm(samplesize, meanlog = model1$estimate[1], sdlog = model1$estimate[2])
fitdistr(bootdata, "lognormal", lower = 0)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
    meanlog       sdlog   
  1.27433563   0.68582472 
 (0.09699026) (0.06858247)
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# c
bootsize <- 1000
bootresult1 <- rep(NA, bootsize)
bootresult2 <- rep(NA, bootsize)
for (i in seq_len(bootsize)) {
  bootdata <- rlnorm(samplesize, meanlog = model1$estimate[1], sdlog = model1$estimate[2])
  modelboot <- fitdistr(bootdata, "lognormal", lower = 0)
  bootresult1[i] <- modelboot$estimate[1]
  bootresult2[i] <- modelboot$estimate[2]
}
quantile(bootresult1, c(0.005, 0.995))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
    0.5%    99.5% 
0.950586 1.464269 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
quantile(bootresult2, c(0.005, 0.995))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
     0.5%     99.5% 
0.5386822 0.8979159 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# We can also compare the SDs of the estimated model parameters
# calculated with and without bootstrap.
model1$sd
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

0.10334753 0.07307774 
```


:::

